Playbook.name: Linux — Attempt to Disable IPTables or Firewall - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: The host firewall was flushed/disabled or its rules changed. RECOVERED: JCB auditd NETFILTER_CFG records firewall rule/config changes (proven live on hq-ameyo hosts), and USER_CMD captures sudo iptables/ufw/firewalld commands. Triage: attacker disabling the firewall, or legitimate firewall administration?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Disabling the host firewall removes a network defense before an attack.

Assets.AssetType: Linux servers (core banking, app, DB - INTDOM)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: JCB Linux auditd does NOT audit execve (no EXECVE records, event.action:exec never occurs) or file paths. It DOES capture: USER_CMD (commands run via sudo, WITH process.args + auditd.log.AUID/UID user), SERVICE_STOP/START (auditd.log.unit), NETFILTER_CFG (firewall config), package events. These queries use those real records.

COVERAGE IS PARTIAL: USER_CMD captures only sudo-invoked commands - it misses actions taken when already root and non-sudo execution. Full coverage requires enabling auditd execve+file auditing (or Elastic Defend / ingesting the already-installed MDE-for-Linux device telemetry).

Signal.Name: Attempt to Disable IPTables or Firewall
Signal.Details: Firewall config change (auditd NETFILTER_CFG) or sudo firewall command (USER_CMD).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the firewall change is an attacker disabling it or legitimate administration.

Step.name: Firewall config changes on the host (NETFILTER_CFG)
Step.Purpose: auditd NETFILTER_CFG records firewall table/rule changes - a burst or a flush is the concern.
Step.Query: FROM logs-auditd.log-* | WHERE auditd.log.record_type == "NETFILTER_CFG" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS changes = COUNT(*), tables = VALUES(auditd.log.table), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Many rapid NETFILTER changes, or a change to the filter table dropping rules, is suspicious. Routine ruleset reloads (e.g. by fail2ban/docker/firewalld on startup) are benign - correlate with the sudo command below.

Step.name: Was a firewall-control command run via sudo
Step.Purpose: A sudo iptables -F / ufw disable / systemctl stop firewalld identifies the actor and the intent (flush/disable).
Step.Query: FROM logs-auditd.log-* | WHERE auditd.log.record_type == "USER_CMD" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cmd = MV_CONCAT(process.args, " ") | WHERE cmd RLIKE "(?i).*(iptables|ip6tables|ufw|firewalld|nft).*" | KEEP @timestamp, auditd.log.AUID, cmd | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A sudo 'iptables -F' (flush), 'ufw disable', or 'systemctl stop firewalld' by an unexpected AUID is the attacker disabling the firewall. A firewall reload under maintenance is benign.

Node.Condition: A firewall flush/disable by an unexpected user, or a rule change dropping protection amid suspicious activity.
Node.Result: True Positive (Firewall Disabled / Defense Evasion - investigate host)

Node.Condition: A routine firewall ruleset reload/maintenance by an admin or a known service.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-NF-CHANGE, INV-02-NF-CMD to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the maintenance/service; close as benign_activity.

TruePositive.Definition: An attacker disabling the host firewall.

SOCAction.Item: Restore the firewall; inspect the host for what the open window allowed; open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A config-management tool cycling firewall rules.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the firewall change and whether protection was removed.
If evasion, restore the firewall and inspect the host.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Restore the firewall; inspect the exposed window; open IR.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enable auditd execve auditing; redesign the detection to use NETFILTER_CFG + USER_CMD; alert on firewall flush/disable.

QualityChecks.Check: RECOVERED via NETFILTER_CFG (firewall config changes) + USER_CMD (sudo iptables/ufw) - proven live. The paired EQL detection cannot fire; redesign it to these records.
Partial: NETFILTER_CFG shows config changes (not always a clean flush signal); USER_CMD catches sudo firewall commands; a direct root iptables call outside sudo may be missed.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Firewall restored; exposed window inspected; host contained.
